### Observed differences

- In the later window, neither A01 nor A02 appears in any of the 200 traces, whereas before, each ran in about 99 of 200 traces (roughly one occurrence per trace). Their relations collapsed with them: A01 co-occurred with A04, A05, A06 or A14 in about half of the earlier traces and never later, and A02's observed handover to A14 is gone. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR002, POS001, POS002, REL001, REL002, REL012]

- Handovers around this segment were rewired. A06 previously passed on to A13 (about 51 in 100 of its outgoing transitions) or A02 (about 49 in 100); in the later window it goes to A14 in all observed cases, typically directly. A13 previously returned to A06 (about 98 in 100) and now goes to A14. A14 itself previously led to A01 and now leads to A08 (about 56 in 100) and A07 (about 35 in 100). [DIR004, DIR010, DIR011, LAG012]

- A new activity, A09, appeared: absent before, it runs in about 47 of 200 later traces, mainly after A07 (about 48 in 100 of A07's outgoing transitions, where A12 previously dominated with about 92 in 100), and continues to A11 (about 46 in 100) and A12 (about 44 in 100). [OCC005, DIR003, DIR005, DIR007, POS005]

- A08 and A10 turned from rare alternatives into a fixed pair. Before, each ran in about a quarter of traces and never together; later, each runs in about half the traces, always together and always A08 before A10. A08's successor changed from A05 to A10, and A05 now follows A08 two positions later instead of immediately, consistent with A10 sitting between them. [OCC004, OCC006, DIR006, REL039, LAG016]

- Repetition and spacing shrank: A06 fell from about two occurrences per trace (in about half the traces) to about 0.5 (in about 36 of 100 traces), and A13 from one occurrence to about 0.4 per trace; several pairs are now closer, e.g. A04 reaches A08 within three steps instead of five, and A14 is immediately before A08 instead of two steps apart. [OCC003, OCC007, LAG003, LAG034]

- A08, A10 and A14 also sit earlier within traces (mean relative position about 0.91 to 0.72, 0.91 to 0.86, and 0.55 to 0.45 respectively); these are event positions, not clock times. [POS004, POS006, POS008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of a structural reorganisation around A01, A02, A06, A13 and A14: the segment A02 → A14 → A01, including A01's branches to A07, A08, A10 and A12, was no longer executed in the later window, and A06 and A13, which previously fed into that segment, now hand over directly to A14, which continues with A08 or A07 instead of A01. The successor changes are observed directly in the direction profiles, participation drops from about half of traces to zero, and every relation profile containing A01 or A02 collapses from co-occurrence to "other activity only" — though these many agreeing relation items largely restate one underlying difference rather than confirming it independently. Chance is implausible as an overall explanation, since 107 items qualified where roughly 0.64 would be expected without change. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR004, DIR010, DIR011, REL001, LAG012]

Other differences: the later window also introduces the new activity A09 after A07 (and occasionally after A04) leading to A11 and A12; A08 and A10, previously rare and mutually exclusive, now form a fixed A08 → A10 pair in about half the traces, replacing A08's immediate handover to A05; A11 now also hands over to A13 in about half of its outgoing transitions; A06 and A13 repeat far less often; and A08, A10 and A14 occupy earlier positions within traces. [OCC005, DIR003, DIR007, DIR006, DIR008, OCC003, POS004]

The evidence cannot rule out that A01 and A02 still exist but were simply not triggered, since zero participation means only non-observation, nor can it distinguish a change within one process from a different mix of cases in the later window; the A04 → A09 link in particular rests on very few observations (about 1 in 100 of A04's outgoing transitions). [OCC001, DIR003]
